problem: Rewrite the expression $({x}^{2}-22x+121)-4$ as the difference between a perfect square and a constant.
worked_solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{x}^{2}-2ax+{a}^{2}=(x-a{)}^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-22x+121 & = \\ {x}^{2}-22x+{11}^{2} & = \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 11x+{11}^{2} & = \\ (x-11{)}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}-22x+121)-4 & = \\ (x-11{)}^{2}-4 & .\end{aligned}
$$
